answer.summary: The strongest foundation is [Severson’s early-cycle prediction](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-019-0356-8), followed by [Attia’s experimental charging optimization](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-1994-5). Voltage, incremental-capacity, resistance and impedance features offer different measurement costs and physical interpretability. Generalization deserves separate evaluation: [varying-usage prediction](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrp.2024.101891) reports 15.1% in-distribution error versus 21.8% extrapolation error. Recent approaches add inter-cell learning, transfer learning, formation-stage prediction and path-dependent degradation models. Charging studies optimize predicted lifetime, an early degradation proxy, or plating potential; cost-aware experimental design additionally decides how long to test. My synthesis is that credible deployment requires operating-condition holdouts and experimental validation alongside prediction accuracy.
gaps: Research gap: broader independent validation across chemistry, temperature, charge/discharge profiles, depth of discharge, manufacturing batches and cell formats remains necessary; the studies cover different subsets.
Research gap: future usage assumptions matter. Conditional capacity forecasts, state-of-health diagnosis, full trajectory prediction and cycle-life endpoints require separate evaluation.
Research gap: nonlinear knees can have weak or electrochemically undetectable precursors, limiting what early-life measurements can reveal.
Research gap: an early feature correlated with lifetime must remain valid when optimization changes the charging protocol and potentially the dominant degradation mechanism.
Research gap: translation from controlled cell experiments to packs and field operation needs treatment of thermal gradients, cell imbalance, sparse diagnostics and changing usage.

Evidence limitation: this review principally screened abstracts and citation metadata; comparative performance was not independently audited from full methods or figures. The two arXiv entries are cited as preprints.

Retrieval limitation: abstracts were unavailable for the Paulson 2022, Geslin 2023, Rhyu 2025 and Sulzer 2021 papers; their quotes are empty. An attempted supplementary publisher-page retrieval also failed.

Coverage limitation: Semantic Scholar search requests timed out and parts of citation expansion were throttled. OpenAlex and arXiv supplied results; the graph omitted some edges, so listed citations are verified but incomplete.
Search date: 2026-10-08. Recent means 2024-10-08 through 2026-10-08, using online publication dates where available. The budget-limited search is selective, not exhaustive.

answer.summary: Early voltage-curve methods predict lifetime before substantial capacity loss; impedance, temperature, formation, and degradation-mode features provide complementary measurements. Closed-loop charging studies use early outcomes to select experiments, while newer cost-aware designs also decide how long each cell should be tested. Generalization is the central limitation: [varying-usage prediction](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrp.2024.101891) reports 15.1% error in distribution versus 21.8% out of distribution, and [uneven-usage impedance forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-32422-w) assumes a known future cycling protocol. Recent inter-cell learning and heterogeneous-data transfer address broader conditions, but [dynamic cycling experiments](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-024-01675-8) show why realistic load profiles must be represented. The papers are ordered by relevance and influence, with recent work identified explicitly.
gaps: Cross-condition performance needs validation that holds out entire operating conditions, manufacturing batches, and chemistries; good prediction within a dataset does not establish universal transfer.
Changing future charge/discharge profiles, temperature, SOC windows, rest periods, and calendar ageing complicate lifetime forecasts; conditional forecasts should state their assumed future use.
Degradation features need physical validation and practical measurement protocols. Features extracted during slow diagnostic charging may not remain identifiable during actual fast charging.
Closed-loop optimization can inherit bias from early lifetime predictors or degradation proxies. Prospective cycle-life confirmation and explicit plating and thermal constraints remain essential.
Formation-stage and heterogeneous-data methods are promising, but independent prospective validation on new industrial cell designs remains a key research need.

Some included papers diagnose degradation or forecast capacity rather than directly predict cycle life; their roles identify this supporting contribution. The Birkl paper is a mechanistic foundation, and the field-data paper is a perspective.

Retrieval limitations: Semantic Scholar search requests timed out and several expansion lookups were throttled. Three publisher-page opens failed. Empty quotes indicate unavailable abstract/text evidence; those reasons are deliberately conservative.
Citation links are only provider-reported reference-list edges between included papers. The expansion truncated its edge output, so the citation list is verified but incomplete.

Search date: 2026-10-08. Recent coverage uses 2024-10-08 through 2026-10-08; arXiv versions are identified separately. Retrieval stayed within eight research operations, counting each native search and page open separately.

answer.summary: Selected 16 papers, prioritizing direct relevance, foundational influence and experimental evidence; eight fall within the requested recent window. Early-life methods extract predictive information from voltage curves, impedance, relaxation or formation measurements before substantial capacity loss. Attia turns early predictions into experimental decisions through Bayesian optimization; newer charging work adds electrochemical constraints and post-mortem validation. Cross-chemistry feature studies, BatLiNet and PBT broaden applicability, but their demonstrated transfer depends on dataset coverage and, in some cases, target labels. Dynamic-cycling experiments show why laboratory accuracy alone cannot establish field validity. These comparisons are a synthesis of the [early-life study](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-019-0356-8), [closed-loop experiments](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-1994-5), [cross-condition prediction](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-024-00972-x) and [dynamic-cycling evidence](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-024-01675-8). Citation links above are limited to relationships directly evidenced in the retrieved text.
gaps: Prospective validation on unseen manufacturers, production batches, chemistries, temperatures and charging protocols remains necessary; random cell splits provide weaker evidence of generalization.
Cycle-life predictions require assumptions about future operation, including dynamic loads, rest periods, calendar ageing and changing charging policies.
Early predictive features may correlate with lifetime without uniquely identifying lithium loss, active-material loss, impedance growth or plating.
Closed-loop optimization needs uncertainty estimates that account for both cell variability and predictor bias, followed by full-life validation of selected protocols.
Laboratory protocols require stronger validation at pack scale, including thermal gradients, cell imbalance and ageing-dependent charging control.
Different end-of-life thresholds, cycle definitions and error metrics hinder comparison; trajectory accuracy does not establish endpoint accuracy.
The eight-call search budget limits completeness, especially for late-2026 publications and citation-network coverage.

answer.summary: Feature-based early-life prediction established the field; combining it with Bayesian experiment selection made charging optimization substantially faster ([Attia et al.](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-1994-5)). Diagnostic and impedance approaches address degradation state and variable usage, while recent inter-cell and transfer methods broaden prediction across conditions ([BatLiNet](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-024-00972-x)). Charging studies increasingly add electrochemical constraints or ageing-model priors, but experimental validation and simulation evidence should be assessed separately. My synthesis: generalization depends on both the operating conditions represented and whether measurements reveal the relevant degradation mechanism. Protocol prediction, intrinsic cell variability and unobservable failure modes require different claims and validation ([feature-selection critique](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.joule.2023.07.021), [2026 limits perspective](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.joule.2026.102423)).
gaps: More prospective tests holding out entire temperatures, charging protocols, chemistries and manufacturing batches, rather than only individual cells.
Better separation of protocol-to-protocol lifetime variation from intrinsic variability among identically operated cells.
Additional sensing for failure modes that lack early electrochemical signatures; model complexity cannot recover an absent signal.
Calibration of prediction uncertainty under changing future usage, with that uncertainty propagated into charging-experiment selection.
More replicated full-life validation of optimized charging on commercial large-format cells and packs, including calendar ageing and thermal variation.
Comparable early-life benchmarks using fixed observation budgets, consistent end-of-life definitions and explicit disclosure of target-domain adaptation data.
Coverage used eight research actions, including one failed page opening; the recent-paper selection and verified citation graph are selective, not exhaustive.

answer.summary: Ranked by relevance, influence, and strength of DAC evidence, rather than citation count alone. Amine-appended MOFs establish strong binding at ambient CO2 partial pressures; newer amine-bearing COFs add convincing humid-air and outdoor-cycling evidence, especially [COF-999](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08080-x) and [COF-1000](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41893-025-01735-1). Ultramicroporous MOFs offer selective physisorption, but water competition and regeneration-induced degradation can undermine dry-gas results, as the [comparative benchmark](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.201506952) shows. Open DAC datasets improve atomistic screening but do not demonstrate cyclic plant performance. Process studies connect coadsorption, kinetics, contactor geometry, climate, and energy supply to cost and net removal. Uptake at roughly 400 ppm should be distinguished from 1,000–10,000 ppm air purification and percent-level flue gas; neither establishes ambient DAC performance by itself.
gaps: Search date: 2026-10-08; recent window: 2024-10-08 through 2026-10-08. Eight research calls were used. Coverage is selective, not exhaustive.

Semantic Scholar search requests timed out, and several citation-expansion requests were throttled. OpenAlex and native web results supplied fallback coverage; the initial arXiv query returned no matches.
The final PMC page opening encountered a CAPTCHA. A defining NbOFFIVE-1-Ni paper was not independently resolved within the budget and is omitted.
Retrieved abstracts were unavailable for the cooperative-insertion and transferable-force-field papers; their quotes are deliberately empty. Some other abstracts were truncated.
ODAC25 sources reported different calculation totals, approximately 60 versus 70 million, likely reflecting versions. No precise total is asserted here.

Important remaining experimental gaps include matched humid-air breakthrough tests near 400 ppm, long-term outdoor aging, amine loss, regeneration durability, and performance after shaping into contactors.

Atomistic adsorption energies and laboratory capacities require validation against multicomponent working capacity, heat and mass transfer, cycle productivity, sorbent manufacture, and complete plant energy balances.
The SIFSIX-18-Ni-β paper is included as a relevant humidity-resistant design contribution, with its 1,000–10,000 ppm concentration boundary explicitly identified.
Citation links are verified examples from returned reference-list edges or explicit abstract references; the graph is incomplete, and missing links do not imply absence of citation.

answer.summary: Amine-appended MOFs and newer chemisorbing COFs provide strong dilute-air evidence, with water enhancing uptake in several systems. COF-999 is especially compelling because it combines 400-ppm measurements with repeated outdoor cycling. Ultramicroporous MOFs offer strong low-pressure physisorption, but the retrieved evidence does not settle their performance under humid ambient air. Computational datasets and screening methods address adsorption chemistry and water competition; predictions still need synthesis, dynamic breakthrough, and regeneration validation. Plant analyses add sorbent lifetime, contactor geometry, cycle duration, manufacture, and energy supply to the evaluation. Percent-level flue-gas or pure-CO₂ uptake cannot substitute for approximately 400-ppm humid-air working capacity. The single citation link is supported by ODAC25's explicit citation of the published ODAC23 work; the listed URL identifies its preprint.
gaps: Search date: 2026-10-08. Eight research operations were used, counting individual web queries and page opens.
Semantic Scholar timed out and later throttled; OpenAlex returned HTTP 429 errors. Citation expansion produced no neighborhood or edges, limiting systematic recovery of influential follow-ups.
Both attempted primary-page opens failed. Several papers resolved bibliographically but lacked accessible abstracts; their quote fields are intentionally empty.
Humid-air cycling, oxygen stability, contaminants, sorbent loss, and shaped-contactor performance remain unevenly documented across the retrieved materials.
Capacity values were measured at different temperatures and humidities and should not be treated as a standardized ranking.
ODAC25 calculation counts differed between retrieved abstract versions; no precise calculation count is asserted.
The 2026 amine-functionalized COF paper was excluded because accessible evidence emphasized 100-kPa uptake and did not sufficiently establish humid-air DAC performance.
Recent preprints and sparse 2026 citation records establish emerging contributions, not independently reproduced performance or mature plant economics.
Additional citation relationships may exist, but none were inferred from topical similarity or shared references.

answer.summary: Ranked by relevance, evidential strength and significance, rather than citation count. Amine-appended MOFs offer strong dilute-CO2 binding and cooperative adsorption, but humid ageing and amine retention matter. Ultramicroporous frameworks offer precise binding sites and rapid physisorption, with water competition a recurring limitation. Recent COFs provide particularly direct evidence from humid 400 ppm and outdoor air. Computational datasets accelerate discovery; optimized cycles and industrial assessments determine whether promising uptake becomes useful net removal. Flue-gas results at percent-level CO2, and trace-stream tests at 1,000–10,000 ppm, cannot establish performance at ambient concentrations. Recent preprints are explicitly labelled. The two citation links are supported respectively by ODAC25’s explicit ODAC23 attribution and the publisher’s citing-literature record.
gaps: More standardized breakthrough and repeated-cycle measurements at approximately 400–430 ppm CO2 in humid air containing oxygen are needed.
Equilibrium uptake, dynamic working capacity and plant productivity remain insufficiently connected across materials studies.
Long-term oxidation, amine loss, hydrolysis and contaminant exposure need testing beyond short laboratory cycling.
Powder performance needs validation after pelletization or coating, including pressure drop, heat transfer and manufacturing cost.
Computational binding-energy datasets need stronger experimental validation for competitive adsorption, kinetics, framework flexibility and degradation.
Plant comparisons need consistent accounting for co-adsorbed water, regeneration, compression, sorbent replacement and net lifecycle removal.
Coverage is selective within eight research-tool calls; failed full-text access limited verification of additional ultramicroporous follow-ups and citation links.

answer.summary: Amine-appended MOFs offer strong dilute-CO2 binding and tunable cooperative adsorption, with humidity, amine retention, and regeneration governing practical performance. COF-999 provides particularly strong recent evidence through 400 ppm humid-air tests and outdoor cycling. Ultramicroporous physisorbents offer selective binding without amines, but water competition remains critical; successful tests at 1,000–10,000 ppm cannot establish ambient-air performance. Open DAC datasets support discovery rather than demonstrated removal. Plant studies show that kinetics, weather, energy supply, sorbent manufacture, and replacement determine cost and net removal. Percent-level flue-gas results should therefore remain separate from ambient-air evidence.
gaps: More standardized breakthrough and working-capacity measurements near 400 ppm across humidity and temperature ranges.
Long-duration outdoor durability, oxidation, contaminant exposure, and amine-loss measurements beyond short cycling campaigns.
Validation of framework powders after shaping into pellets, monoliths, or contactors, including pressure drop and heat transfer.
Experimental validation of computational rankings under competitive adsorption, cooperative chemistry, and realistic regeneration.
Transparent plant operating data linking measured sorbent lifetime to net-removal cost and life-cycle emissions.
The eight-call search supports a selective bibliography; comprehensive coverage of late-2026 experiments and citation links remains unverified.

answer.summary: The central lineage is human comparisons → learned reward model → PPO policy optimization, which DPO reformulates as offline classification using reference-relative policy probabilities. IPO and GPO generalize the objective; ODPO, TDPO, APO, and DiscoPOP alter margins, granularity, update control, or loss design. ORPO and SimPO remove the reference model, while KTO removes the paired-data requirement but retains a reference. SLiC-HF and RRHF are earlier parallel alternatives. Zephyr established an accessible DPO recipe; recent Tülu 3 and OLMo 2 recipes combine SFT, DPO, and verifiable-reward RL at scale. IPO changes the loss to squared target-margin regression; ORPO combines supervised likelihood with odds-ratio preferences; SimPO uses length-normalized rewards without a reference model; KTO accepts unpaired binary feedback. answer.summary: The strongest starting sequence is DeepSeekMath, DeepSeek-R1, Dr. GRPO, DAPO, GSPO, and SAPO. Original GRPO uses prompt-group centered, standard-deviation-normalized rewards with token-level PPO clipping, per-response token averaging, and a reference-policy KL penalty. Dr. GRPO addresses length bias; DAPO combines asymmetric clipping and token aggregation with sampling and reward changes; GSPO moves update control to sequences; SAPO uses soft gates. GDPO, BNPO, KRPO, PAPO, and CorrGRPO change reward or advantage construction. Recent theory distinguishes useful adaptive normalization, aggregation bias, and the tradeoff between unbiased gradients and length-invariant contributions. AReaL and HybridFlow primarily change training execution. This ordering reflects relevance and influence, not a cross-paper performance ranking: model initialization, data, rollout budgets, decoding, verifiers, and evaluation estimators differ.
gaps: Search date: 2026-10-08. Both pre-window foundations and papers within 2024-10-08–2026-10-08 are included; very recent preprints have limited independent validation.
Eight research calls were used, counting each opened page separately. Semantic Scholar searches timed out, and citation expansion was heavily throttled; the newest-paper coverage is incomplete.
Only one within-list citation was unambiguously verified against viewed text. Similarity, shared references, and mentions without verified bibliography mappings were excluded from citation links.
Several abstracts were truncated to 1,000 characters. Quotes use only retrieved verbatim text; detailed assumptions and complete ablations were not verified for every paper.

Controlled comparisons should match base checkpoints, training tokens and compute, group size, truncation, reward implementation, and decoding. DAPO's reported avg@32 should not be conflated with pass@32.
Generalization beyond mathematical reasoning, interactions between objective and asynchronous execution changes, and multi-seed stability remain important comparison gaps.

answer.summary:
Ordered by foundational importance and direct relevance, not cross-paper benchmark scores. For outcome rewards, original GRPO uses a within-prompt standardized advantage, token-level clipped importance ratios, per-response token averaging, and a reference-policy KL penalty. Dr. GRPO removes response-length and reward-standard-deviation normalization. DAPO instead uses token aggregation, asymmetric clipping and overlong reward shaping, alongside dynamic sampling and an open training system. These are different weighting choices, with different biases. [GRPO and DAPO formulations](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.14476v2).

GSPO changes the importance-ratio and clipping unit; CISPO clips importance weights; SAPO smooths update suppression. Reward-estimation approaches change a different component: global normalization, Beta normalization, median baselines, Bayesian shrinkage, or multi-reward normalization. Recent theory argues that normalization can help convergence and that gradient unbiasedness differs from length-invariant trajectory influence. These claims depend on their respective assumptions.

AReaL and INTELLECT-2 primarily address execution and infrastructure, while also involving training recipes; asynchronous policy staleness connects system design back to stability. Their throughput results cannot establish objective superiority.

Compare algorithms only with matched base checkpoints, training data, verifiers, rollout counts, token and compute budgets, truncation rules, evaluation sampling, metrics and seeds. DAPO reports avg@32, meaning average sampled accuracy; pass@32 measures success among 32 attempts. No benchmark scores from incompatible setups are ranked here.
gaps: Search date: 2026-10-08; eight research calls used. DeepSeekMath is included as a foundation outside the 2024-10-08–2026-10-08 recent window.

Semantic Scholar searches timed out and citation expansion was throttled. OpenAlex, arXiv and native search supplied coverage, but influence rankings are qualitative rather than a verified citation-count ranking.

Only one citation edge between listed primary URLs was directly verified in the returned graph. Other relationships are omitted because method mentions and topical similarity do not establish reference-list citations.
Several 2026 contributions are recent preprints. Their abstracts establish the proposed contributions, but this review did not independently verify proofs, implementation details or replication.
The length-bias literature uses several meanings of bias: gradient-estimator bias, equal trajectory influence, token weighting and observed verbosity. A common controlled evaluation remains needed.
Uniform-reward remedies change sampling, baselines or the learning target in different ways; evidence is still needed under matched rollout costs, correlated samples and verifier noise.
General RLHF frameworks, multimodal-only applications, training-free agents and unrelated uses of GRPO were excluded. Coverage of very recent work may be limited by indexing delays.

answer.summary: Ordered by foundational importance and direct relevance, rather than cross-paper benchmark scores. Original GRPO uses within-prompt standardized rewards, token-level clipped ratios, per-response token averaging, and reference-policy KL regularization. [DeepSeekMath](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.03300) establishes the method; [R1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948) establishes its large-scale reasoning application. [Dr. GRPO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783) changes length and reward normalization. [DAPO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14476) changes clipping and loss aggregation while also changing sampling, truncation rewards, data, and implementation; its gains therefore concern a combined recipe. [GSPO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18071) changes importance weighting and clipping, retaining group reward normalization; its infrastructure benefits follow from that objective change. GDPO addresses multiple reward components, while GMPO, GTPO, and recent robust-estimation work target different instability mechanisms. Their reported scores do not establish a universal ranking: Dr. GRPO's small-model experiments, DAPO's Qwen2.5-32B setup, and GSPO's cold-start Qwen3 MoE setup differ in models, data, decoding, and compute.

Sampling filters, truncation handling, data changes, routing replay, and inference-training probability discrepancies need separate ablations from objective changes.
Binary-reward normalization analyses should not be generalized automatically to continuous, noisy, or multiple rewards; dense-model stability results likewise need separate MoE validation.
Recent September 2026 proposals have limited time for independent replication and should not yet be treated as established successors.

answer.summary: Ordered by direct relevance and established influence, rather than benchmark scores; all entries except foundational DeepSeekMath fall within the requested two-year window. Original GRPO uses A_i=(R_i−mean(R))/std(R), averages a clipped token surrogate within each response, and adds KL regularization. Dr. GRPO changes length and advantage normalization; DAPO combines clipping and aggregation changes with sampling and reward interventions. GSPO changes the ratio and clipping unit, retaining group normalization and using a length-normalized sequence ratio; CISPO and SAPO modify how updates are restricted. GDPO addresses multiple reward components, while GFPO changes which sampled responses receive training. IcePop changes gradient weighting to address engine mismatch; C3PO++ and ASystem address rollout execution and infrastructure. Recent theory qualifies claims that removing normalization universally improves optimization or eliminates every notion of length bias. These distinctions are supported by [Dr. GRPO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783), [GSPO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18071), and [the length-weighting analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23364). No cross-paper performance ranking is inferred: compare matched initialization, data, reward verifier, architecture, rollout compute, decoding, token limits, and metrics. In particular, sampled average pass@1, greedy accuracy, pass@k, and voting accuracy are different evaluations.
gaps: The eight-call research budget supports a selective reading list and partial verified citation graph, not an exhaustive survey or measured citation-impact ranking.
Recent 2026 theoretical claims need independent replication and careful checking of their assumptions; they should not be treated as universal prescriptions.
Matched comparisons jointly varying normalization, clipping, reward shaping, group size, and engine mismatch remain needed to isolate their effects.
Length studies should report correctness versus total training and inference compute, including discarded rollouts, rather than response length alone.
Stability results need repeated seeds, collapse rates, and separate dense-model, MoE, synchronous, and asynchronous evaluations.
Evidence is concentrated in verifiable mathematics and coding; transfer to open-ended reasoning, imperfect verifiers, and multi-turn tasks remains less established.

answer.summary: Late interaction retains fine-grained token evidence, with storage and search costs addressed by residual compression, pruning, and specialized engines such as [WARP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17788). Learned sparse retrieval produces weighted vocabulary vectors for inverted indexes, but learned posting distributions still require specialized traversal or approximate search, exemplified by [Seismic](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.18812). Matryoshka-style compression offers another route by reducing embedding dimensionality. Evaluate effectiveness and measured latency, memory, and recall together; use BEIR for domain transfer and newer benchmarks for multilingual, instructed, or reasoning-intensive retrieval. These are first-stage retrieval methods or evaluation/compression contributions. Cross-encoder reranking is a separate downstream stage; late-interaction candidate rescoring, including SPLATE's pipeline, is not cross-encoder reranking.
gaps: Search date: 2026-10-08. Used eight research calls, counting the two final page opens separately. Recent means first public release between 2024-10-08 and 2026-10-08.
Semantic Scholar searches partly timed out, and citation expansion encountered throttling. Several mismatched index records were discarded; coverage and citation counts are incomplete.

Citation links come from provider reference-list edges or explicit citations in retrieved primary text. The ColBERT DOI record was normalized to its matching arXiv URL. Missing links do not imply absence of a citation.
The 25-paper ceiling leaves additional follow-ups, including SPLADE++, CITADEL, EMVB, and SeismicWave, outside this selection; their full comparison was not verified within the budget.
Recent preprint mechanisms were checked through abstracts, but implementation quality, reproducibility, and performance claims were not independently audited.

Hardware-normalized efficiency, tail latency, index construction and update costs, long-document behavior, and quality after combined compression remain important comparison gaps. Benchmark effectiveness scores alone cannot establish deployment efficiency.

answer.summary: Late interaction preserves token-level matching but needs compression and efficient candidate processing; ColBERTv2, PLAID, XTR, and WARP address these costs. Learned sparse retrieval uses lexical representations and inverted indexes, with efficiency depending on encoder cost, expansion, pruning, and index organization. JPQ compresses dense indexes; Matryoshka and SMEC reduce embedding dimensionality. BEIR evaluates retrieval generalization, while MTEB/MMTEB provide broader embedding evaluation. Cross-encoder rerankers are excluded from the paper list; SPLATE’s subsequent ColBERT scoring remains late interaction. Citation links come from Lens reference edges or explicit citations in primary text.

answer.summary: Ranked by relevance and foundational value, rather than citation counts. Late interaction preserves token-level detail; learned sparse retrieval supports inverted-index search. Compression reduces storage, while pruning and optimized scoring reduce retrieval work. Evaluate quality alongside full query latency and index size, using BEIR for generalization, BRIGHT for reasoning, and CoRECT for compression at scale. These methods support first-stage retrieval; cross-encoders jointly process query–document candidates for reranking. Cross-encoder supervision does not change a retriever’s inference architecture. Recent means first release within 2024-10-08–2026-10-08. All listed citation edges are explicitly supported by [WARP’s bibliography](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.17788v2#bib).

answer.summary:
The main change during 2025-04-08–2026-10-08 was the move from impressive deterministic research forecasts toward operational probabilistic systems and transferable atmospheric models. GraphCast’s graph network and Pangu’s 3D transformer established the earlier deterministic breakthrough; GenCast’s December 2024 diffusion result and AIFS Single’s February 2025 launch set the stage just before this 18-month window.

Evaluation changed with the objective. Deterministic comparisons emphasize RMSE and anomaly correlation against ECMWF HRES. GenCast instead evaluated 50-member ensembles against historical 2019 ENS, regridded to 0.25°, using CRPS, calibration, extreme-event probabilities, and downstream applications. Its protocol verified each system against its corresponding analysis and addressed assimilation-window look-ahead; precipitation was excluded from headline results. Consequently, “97.4% of targets” means winning variable–level–lead-time comparisons, not 97.4% forecast accuracy or a comparison with today’s ENS. [GenCast protocol](https://arxiv.org/html/2312.15796v2).

Diffusion generates atmospheric states through iterative denoising. AIFS-CRPS and FGN learn stochastic ensembles directly with proper-score objectives, reducing sampling work; FGN also demonstrates joint spatial structure despite marginal training. FourCastNet 3 adds a spherical convolutional alternative. Aurora and Prithvi pursue a different axis: broad pretraining followed by task adaptation. Aurora’s atmospheric-composition comparison uses CAMS, while Prithvi’s gravity-wave transfer concerns parameterization rather than an HRES forecast contest. [Aurora](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09005-y), [Prithvi](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.13598).

Operational status is explicit: ECMWF launched AIFS Single on 25 February 2025 and AIFS ENS on 1 July 2025 alongside physics-based IFS. Google released the FGN-based WeatherNext 2 as a deployed forecast product in November 2025. These deployments are distinct from retrospective research results or publicly released weights. [ECMWF deployment dates](https://www.ecmwf.int/en/newsletter/186/news/machine-learning-services-ecmwf-new-capabilities-users), [WeatherNext 2 launch](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-deepmind/weathernext-2/). Independent extreme-event studies qualify average-skill gains: the tested deterministic AI systems still struggle with record-breaking events.
gaps: Search date: 2026-10-08. Eight research calls were used. This is a selected literature map, not exhaustive coverage.
Semantic Scholar search and expansion requests were throttled; OpenAlex, arXiv, and native primary-source search supplied the remaining evidence.

The GenCast Nature full-text page was inaccessible. Detailed verification and reference evidence came from its May 2024 arXiv version; the December 2024 publication’s metadata and abstract were verified separately.

Recent papers were generally screened through abstracts, some truncated to 1,000 characters. Full experimental protocols for every ensemble model were not audited; September 2026 work remains preliminary.

ECMWF comparisons differ in forecast cycle, resolution, initialization, verifying analysis, ensemble size, and test years. Historical benchmark wins do not establish superiority over the October 2026 operational IFS.
Marginal CRPS does not fully establish joint multivariate calibration, conservation, realistic extremes, or downstream decision value; those require additional verification.
The record-breaking-extremes study tested named deterministic AI models. Its conclusions should not automatically be extended to newer diffusion or CRPS-trained ensembles.

Foundation-model transfer results do not establish universal superiority across Earth-system tasks. Online stability of learned parameterizations and performance outside the training climate remain open questions.
Operational deployments were verified for ECMWF AIFS and Google WeatherNext 2. Deployment status of other listed models was not established.

Citation links use returned reference-list edges or explicit GenCast citations. Identified preprint/publication variants were consolidated; similarity and shared references were not treated as citations.

answer.summary:
The main change during 2025-04-08–2026-10-08 is maturation from deterministic forecast demonstrations into operational uncertainty prediction and transferable Earth-system modeling. GraphCast's mesh graphs and Pangu's atmospheric transformer established deterministic skill against ECMWF HRES; error-minimizing predictions nevertheless tend to smooth uncertain small-scale structures. GenCast samples atmospheric trajectories through diffusion, whereas AIFS-CRPS learns stochastic members by directly optimizing a probabilistic score. Aurora takes a complementary route: diverse pretraining followed by task-specific fine-tuning for weather, atmospheric chemistry and waves.

Operational status is clearest at ECMWF: AIFS Single entered operations on 25 February 2025, just before the 18-month window; the 51-member, CRPS-trained AIFS ENS followed on 1 July 2025. Both reached version 2 on 12 May 2026. The earlier diffusion-based AIFS ensemble was experimental. These systems run alongside physics-based IFS. [ECMWF operational dates and versions](https://www.ecmwf.int/en/forecasts/datasets/aifs-machine-learning-data), [ensemble deployment](https://www.ecmwf.int/en/about/media-centre/news/2025/ecmwfs-ensemble-ai-forecasts-become-operational). Research comparisons against operational systems do not themselves establish deployment; ECMWF's daily runs of external models were separately described as external-model activity. [ECMWF account](https://www.ecmwf.int/en/about/media-centre/aifs-blog/2026/farewell-external-ai-models).

Baseline details materially affect the conclusions. GenCast compared equal 50-member ensembles against 2019 ENS, regridded to 0.25°, using each system's corresponding analysis and accounting for assimilation look-ahead. Its 97.4% result concerns CRPS targets, excludes precipitation from the headline scorecard, and does not establish that margin against today's 9-km ENS. [GenCast evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.15796). Aurora's evaluations use RMSE/ACC and task-specific ECMWF baselines: IFS for weather, CAMS for chemistry and HRES-WAM for waves. [Aurora](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13063). Observation-based verification provides a necessary counterweight: the 2026 operational wind study found raw IFS superior to raw AIFS at stations. [Station evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.02508).
gaps: Current-cycle comparisons remain incomplete: results against historical HRES or ENS configurations cannot be read as wins against October 2026 ECMWF systems.
More independent verification is needed against stations, radar and satellite observations, particularly for precipitation intensity, monsoons, cyclone intensity and rare extremes.
Good marginal CRPS and realistic spectra do not guarantee correct joint distributions, physical conservation, coupled Earth-system behavior or decision value.
Most learned forecasting systems still depend on physics-based analyses and reanalyses; Aardvark addresses this dependence experimentally, without establishing an operational replacement.

Operational deployment of every external or commercial model was not verified. The eight-search/opening budget also limits completeness of the 2026 literature and citation graph; empty quotes indicate no verified excerpt.

answer.summary: Ranked by foundational importance, influence, and direct relevance rather than unreliable citation totals. Separate-model drafting, self-speculation, feature-based drafting, multiple heads, and diffusion drafting primarily change proposal cost and accuracy. Exactness comes from verification: standard speculative sampling accepts using min(1,p/q) and corrects rejections with the normalized positive residual of p−q. Matching greedy outputs alone does not establish preservation of stochastic sampling. Trees additionally require correct ancestor-only attention, positions, and acceptance accounting; optimizing tree size is separate from optimizing acceptance. Block Verification and optimal-transport methods improve acceptance while retaining distribution constraints. [Medusa](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10774) offers both corrected sampling and approximate typical acceptance; Fuzzy Speculative Decoding explicitly permits distributional deviation. LayerSkip's verification is relative to its trained checkpoint. Recent highlights include EAGLE-3, DFlash, multi-draft acceptance bounds, and overlapping drafting with verification. Citation links come from Citation Lens reference-list edges or explicit Medusa in-text citations.

answer.summary: Exact stochastic decoding requires an acceptance-and-resampling rule that preserves the target distribution; preserving the greedy token sequence is a separate guarantee. The foundational methods establish exact sampling, while multi-head, feature-based, self-speculative, and diffusion drafters chiefly change proposal cost and quality. Tree methods broaden candidate coverage but require ancestor-correct attention and proposal-aware verification; joint block and transport-based verification improve how candidates are accepted. Medusa explicitly supports both exact rejection sampling and approximate typical acceptance; SPRINTER and Approximate Speculative Decoding relax verification or token agreement. Exactness is relative to the chosen target checkpoint and numerical implementation. See [speculative sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.01318), [Medusa](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10774), and [block verification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10444).

answer.summary:
The main advances during April 2025–October 2026 concern memory editing, transition expressivity, hardware utilization, and production-scale hybridization. Gated DeltaNet combines broad forgetting with a corrective write that replaces an existing key–value association rather than merely accumulating another outer product. Kimi Delta Attention adds channel-wise forgetting; FG²-GDN and Gated DeltaNet-2 further refine update rates and separate erasure from writing. These changes principally target associative recall and interference in compressed memory. [Gated DeltaNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06464), [Kimi Linear](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26692), [Gated DeltaNet-2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22791).

State tracking requires composing operations, beyond remembering facts. Negative-eigenvalue results identify limitations of positive-only transitions; DeltaProduct increases transition expressivity through multiple updates. Mamba-3 combines improved discretization, complex-valued transitions, and MIMO computation. At 1.5B scale, its reported MIMO gain over Gated DeltaNet is 1.8 percentage points; its hardware strategy adds useful computation during memory-bound decoding. These are controlled research results, with synthetic-task and scale limitations. [Negative eigenvalues](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.12537), [DeltaProduct](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10297), [Mamba-3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15569).

Production adoption favors hybrids. Qwen3-Next, released September 2025 at 80B total/3B active parameters, uses three Gated DeltaNet layers per full-attention layer. Its official technical blog is a primary deployment source, but is not counted as a paper here. Kimi Linear combines KDA with full MLA; Nemotron-H and Nemotron 3 combine Mamba with attention and increasingly extensive MoE and inference optimizations. Full attention supplies direct access to token history that fixed recurrent memory cannot preserve arbitrarily. [Qwen3-Next release](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3-next), [Kimi Linear](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26692), [Nemotron 3 Super](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12374).

Pure recurrent mixers have linear sequence-processing cost and sequence-length-independent decoding state at fixed model size. Hybrids retaining global attention still have quadratic attention prefill and growing KV caches, although fewer attention layers substantially reduce their constants. Production throughput claims come from technical reports and combine architecture, kernels, precision, MoE, and speculative decoding; they do not isolate the recurrence's contribution. The strongest peer-reviewed mechanism evidence comes from GLA, DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet, the state-tracking papers, and Mamba-3.

Qwen3-Next is documented through its official release blog. A dedicated paper was not verified; the ordinary Qwen3 Technical Report should not be substituted for its hybrid architecture.
The August 2026 Qwen3.8-Next item was verified only through indexed abstract material. Its experimental details, release status, and peer-review status remain unchecked.
Peer-review status was not established for RWKV-7 or Griffin. Recent FG²-GDN and Gated DeltaNet-2 claims are treated as preprint evidence.

Cross-model speedups require matched hardware, precision, batch size, context length, output length, and quality. Production reports rarely isolate all of these or separate recurrence gains from MoE and speculative decoding.

Synthetic state-tracking capability does not establish reliable long-horizon code execution, agent state management, or multilingual reasoning. Fixed-state recall capacity and length generalization remain important limitations.
Sparse attention, exact-attention acceleration, vision-only applications, and September 2026 Mamba-3 tracking extensions without demonstrated language-model results were outside the core scope.

answer.summary:
The strongest change during April 2025–October 2026 is better management of compressed recurrent memory, coupled with deployment in large attention hybrids. Selective SSMs choose what to retain; Mamba-2 makes their computation hardware-efficient. GLA adds feature-dependent forgetting to additive matrix memory. DeltaNet instead corrects the association addressed by the current key; Gated DeltaNet combines that targeted correction with forgetting. KDA makes decay channel-wise, while the April–May 2026 FG²-GDN and Gated DeltaNet-2 papers refine per-channel updates and separate erasure from writing. These changes primarily address associative recall and interference. State tracking requires a different improvement: negative eigenvalues, richer Householder products, or complex transitions, as illustrated by the state-tracking papers, RWKV-7, and Mamba-3.

Production-scale evidence favors hybrids: Nemotron-H and Nemotron 3 combine Mamba with attention; Kimi Linear combines KDA with full MLA and reports up to 75% less KV cache and 6× decoding throughput at 1M context under its evaluated conditions. Those gains are technical-report results, whereas GDN and Mamba-3 have conference publication evidence. The 2026 Nemotron 3 Super report also adds low-precision training, MoE changes, and speculative decoding, so its throughput gains cannot be attributed to recurrence alone. Qwen3-Next and Qwen3.5 are relevant released gated-delta/attention hybrids documented in their [official Qwen3-Next model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct) and [official Qwen3.5 model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B); these release documents are separate from the paper list. Pure fixed-state recurrences offer constant memory and constant work per decoded token at fixed model dimensions. Hybrids retaining global attention still have growing KV caches and quadratic full-attention prefill components, even when their practical costs are substantially reduced.

Ranked by direct relevance and strength of evidence, rather than citation counts. Eight research calls were used; citation edges are supported by inspected references or explicit in-text citations. Empty quotes indicate that a suitable passage from that paper was not retrieved.

Over April 2025–October 2026, the main changes concern memory editing, state dynamics and deployment. Gating controls memory lifetime; delta updates correct the association under a particular key instead of simply accumulating another write. Gated DeltaNet combines these operations, Kimi Delta Attention makes forgetting channel-wise, and Gated DeltaNet-2 separately controls erasing and writing. The latter's promising retrieval results remain 1.3B-scale experiments. [Gated DeltaNet-2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22791).

Selective SSMs also advanced: Mamba-3 introduces richer discretization, complex-valued dynamics for state tracking and MIMO computation. It reports comparable perplexity to Mamba-2 with half the state size; its main controlled language experiments are substantially smaller than production hybrids. [Mamba-3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15569).

Production designs retain full attention for global retrieval. Kimi's 3:1 KDA–MLA stack reports up to 75% less KV cache and approximately 6× decoding throughput at 1M context against its matched MLA baseline. MiniMax-01 and Nemotron-H represent other interleaved families; Falcon-H1 combines mechanisms within layers. Qwen3-Next's adoption of Gated DeltaNet is recorded by the implementation authors. [Kimi Linear](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26692), [FLA](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention).

The 2026 Nemotron Super/Ultra reports demonstrate much larger deployment, but their throughput combines recurrence, MoE, precision and speculative decoding. Ultra's reported advantage changes from roughly 6× against GLM-5.1 to 1.6× against Qwen3.5, with different serving stacks. These are technical-report comparisons, not isolated recurrence ablations. [Nemotron 3 Ultra](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15007).

Fixed-state recurrent layers have constant history memory and linear sequence cost. Hybrids containing global full attention still have quadratic asymptotic prefill cost and growing KV caches, with smaller constants.

answer.summary: The main 2025–26 advance is better memory management plus deployment at scale. Selective SSMs use input-dependent dynamics; delta rules correct particular key–value associations; Gated DeltaNet adds rapid forgetting to those corrections, improving recall and context switching ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06464)). KDA makes forgetting channel-wise and supplies specialized chunkwise kernels. Kimi Linear interleaves three KDA layers with one global MLA layer, reporting up to 75% less KV cache and sixfold decoding throughput at 1M context; larger feasible batches contribute to that gain ([report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26692)). Qwen3-Next independently deploys a 3:1 Gated DeltaNet/full-attention hybrid with sparse MoE; its official release description is a blog, so it is excluded from the paper list ([release](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3-next)). Nemotron-H demonstrates the corresponding Mamba–Transformer production path ([report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.03624)). Mamba-3 improves state tracking through complex-valued updates and improves performance without higher decode latency through MIMO; its principal reported comparison is at 1.5B scale ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15569)). Pure recurrent layers have sequence-length-independent decode state and work. Hybrids retain growing attention caches and quadratic full-attention prefill components. Production efficiency claims primarily come from technical reports; foundational algorithms and Mamba-3 have peer-reviewed evidence.
gaps: The eight-action budget limits completeness, especially for later 2026 production releases; Qwen3.5 and Nemotron 3 architecture reports were not verified.
Several entries have empty quotes because their own abstract or text was not retrieved; publication status is explicitly unresolved where verification was unavailable.
Fixed-size recurrent memory still faces interference and capacity limits; synthetic associative recall does not establish reliable retrieval across arbitrary million-token documents.
State-tracking gains need evaluation on persistent variable updates, revisions, tool interactions and long reasoning trajectories beyond small synthetic tasks.
Cross-family efficiency comparisons need matched training data, active parameters, quality, hardware, precision, batch size and separate prefill/decode measurements.
Sparse MoE, distillation, quantization and serving kernels confound production speedups; recurrence-only gains require controlled ablations.

answer.summary: Table detection locates table regions on pages; structure recognition recovers cells, row/column membership and spans; OCR recognizes cell characters, which must then be assigned to the recovered cells. These tasks require separate measurements as well as pipeline evaluation. Table Transformer predicts structural components using object detection; TableFormer predicts structure plus cell boxes; UniTable jointly models structure, boxes and text. GraphTSR predicts cell relationships, LORE regresses logical coordinates, and TSRFormer/SEMv3/TABLET construct and merge grids. SPRINT offers an alternative structure language, while TFLOP directly associates text regions with structure. The strongest recent additions verified here are TABLET, the VLLM recognition benchmark, and the two 2026 evaluation papers. The latter emphasize diagnostic and end-to-end evaluation. See [PubTables-1M](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.00061), [UniTable](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04822), and [the 2026 extraction benchmark](https://doi.org/10.1145/3770855.3817462).
gaps: Annotation conventions affect measured performance: PubTables-1M identifies oversegmentation, and Aligning benchmark datasets demonstrates gains from correcting errors and inconsistencies with a fixed model. Scores across unaligned datasets therefore need caution. Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.00061 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.00716.

Dataset provenance limits coverage: PubTabNet comes from scientific articles in PubMed Central, while TableBank uses Word/LaTeX documents. Broad generalization beyond those sources is an inference requiring external testing. WTW and cTDaR add deformation and historical-document challenges.

Input assumptions differ: GraphTSR starts with supplied cells; TableFormer can obtain text from programmatic PDFs. Neither setting alone establishes performance when cells and text must both be recovered from scans.

Crop-level structure evaluation misses detection failures. The 2026 extraction benchmark also identifies positive-only evaluation as a source of inflated precision. Its own scope is text-based scientific PDFs, explicitly excluding scans to avoid additional OCR errors. Source: https://doi.org/10.1145/3770855.3817462.

FormStruct-Bench covers hierarchical table-form documents and uses 70 reusable templates expanded into verified instances. Its diagnostic results should not be treated as interchangeable with conventional table-grid benchmarks. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10396.
Publication dates require care: TFLOP and SPRINT have 2025 arXiv deposits but earlier 2024 conference versions; they are treated as follow-ups. UniTable and SEMv3 first appeared before 2024-10-08.

Search completed for the 2026-10-08 cutoff using eight research calls. Semantic Scholar search timed out and several expansion lookups were throttled; some returned metadata was inconsistent. Citation coverage is consequently partial, and similarity links were excluded.

The 2026 TDATR paper surfaced in search, but its primary PDF returned HTTP 403; it was excluded rather than assigned an unverified supporting quote. This bounded search does not establish exhaustive coverage of 2025–2026 methods.

answer.summary: Ordered by relevance and foundational value, without claiming a citation-count ranking. Detection locates table regions on pages; structure recognition recovers cells, rows, columns, spans, and their geometry; OCR recognizes cell text. Table Transformer treats detection and structure as object detection, while TableFormer generates structure and localizes cells, obtaining text separately. LORE regresses logical cell positions; TRUST splits and merges grids; ClusterTabNet predicts word relations. Recent directions add language guidance or compact serialization. [PubTables-1M](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.00061), [TableFormer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01017), [LORE](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v37i3.25402), [Cell-Code](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patrec.2025.07.022). Recent-window labels use venue publication dates; they do not establish when a method first appeared.
gaps: Domain coverage: PubTables-1M explicitly contains scientific-article tables. Transfer to camera images, degraded scans, and other document domains needs separate testing; this is an inference from its source distribution. [PubTables-1M](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.00061).

Annotation comparability: SEMv2 reports correcting SciTSR test annotations and explicitly cautions that comparisons with other methods may therefore be unfair. Scores from differently corrected test sets should not be pooled. [SEMv2 manuscript](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372332012_SEMv2_Table_Separation_Line_Detection_Based_on_Instance_Segmentation).

Representation limits: the TSG paper identifies ambiguity in existing representations for nested spans, vacancies, and slanted headers. Benchmark accuracy can therefore depend on what the target representation can express. [TSG](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2025.108352).

Evaluation separation: report detection, cell geometry/topology, and OCR independently alongside end-to-end results. TableFormer's use of PDF-source text means its content-extraction setting does not directly establish OCR performance on scanned images. [TableFormer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01017).

Semantic difficulty: UniTabNet identifies descriptive textual cells as a weakness of predominantly visual methods, motivating evaluations that vary textual semantics as well as geometry. [UniTabNet](https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2024.findings-emnlp.355).

Research coverage: eight search/open operations were used, counting the three initial searches separately. Two PDF retrievals failed; some foundational entries consequently have empty quotes. No 2026 paper was verified, and TSG's exact publication date remains unchecked, so coverage through 2026-10-08 is incomplete.

papers.reason: Develops visual-alignment coordinate modeling and reports improvements over TableFormer using structure-only evaluation.
papers.quote: Compared with the strong baseline TableFormer, VAST improved the S-TEDS score by 1.83% on FinTabNet and 0.48% on PubTabNet.

papers.title: Towards One-Stage End-to-End Table Structure Recognition with Parallel Regression for Diverse Scenarios
papers.role: Recent alternative model; TableCenterNet; April 2025 preprint
papers.reason: Replaces sequential decoding and elaborate reconstruction with parallel prediction of cells' spatial and logical positions.
papers.quote: This network unifies the prediction of table spatial and logical structure into a parallel regression task for the first time

papers.title: FastTab: A Fast Table Recognizer with a Tiny Recursive Module and 1D Transformers
papers.role: Recent efficiency-oriented alternative; May 2026 preprint
papers.reason: Combines global recursive reasoning with axial transformers in a grid-based recognizer; its impact remains emerging.
papers.quote: We introduce FastTab, a grid-centric TSR model that avoids autoregressive HTML decoding

answer.summary: Ranked by relevance and historical importance, rather than measured citation counts. Table detection locates table regions on a page; cell structure recognition recovers rows, columns, spans, and geometry; OCR recognizes characters inside cells. These require separate evaluation. TATR detects structural objects and requires separately supplied text; TableFormer combines transformer structure decoding with cell localization. TRUST and TSRFormer predict separators and merge cells. TableCenterNet offers parallel spatial/logical regression, while FastTab uses a grid representation. PubTables-v2 adds page-level object relationships and multi-page evaluation. The three recent entries fall within 2024-10-08–2026-10-08. Sources: [TATR documentation](https://github.com/microsoft/table-transformer/blob/main/README.md), [TableFormer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01017), [PubTables-v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10888).
gaps: Annotation ambiguity: PubTables-1M identifies oversegmentation as a source of inconsistent ground truth. Benchmark improvements can therefore reflect annotation corrections as well as model improvements. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.00061

Cropped-table evaluation omits detection and page context. PubTables-v2 reports that PubTabNet and PubTables-1M structure annotations cover cropped tables; it also flags missing page-level tables in FinTabNet. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10888

Potential leakage: PubTables-v2 identifies incompatible document splits in a dataset combining PubLayNet and PubTables-1M, and introduces hidden test data to help assess future contamination. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10888

OCR comparisons need matched inputs: PubTables-v2 supplies underlying PDF text to TATR, whereas its evaluated VLMs must recognize text visually. Content scores therefore measure different pipelines. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10888

Metrics are not interchangeable: TEDS includes cell content; structure-only TEDS excludes it. Cell-adjacency benchmarks also differ in whether they match cells using text or geometric overlap. Source: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2023/papers/Huang_Improving_Table_Structure_Recognition_With_Visual-Alignment_Sequential_Coordinate_Modeling_CVPR_2023_paper.pdf

Domain coverage remains limited: scientific articles and PDF-rendered images do not establish performance on degraded scans, handwriting, or multilingual business documents. This is an inference from the documented dataset construction, not a measured result across all listed models.

Research coverage is selective: the eight-operation budget included failed retrievals. Empty quote fields indicate that original paper text was not retrieved; recent preprints should not be treated as established influential works.

papers.role: Recent preprint; 2026-07-08; second-order weight PTQ
papers.reason: Adds gradient covariance to activation covariance, addressing unequal output-channel sensitivity omitted by common reconstruction objectives.
papers.quote: Under the Kronecker-factored Hessian approximation, the quantization loss depends jointly on both the activation and gradient covariances

papers.quote: AAAC replaces the fixed scalar codebook used in standard quantization with two small learned scalar codebooks (64 bytes) per layer.

papers.role: Newest preprint; 2026-10-03; weight-only; codebook refinement

papers.quote: improves quantization quality through balanced fitting of existing codebooks.

answer.summary: Ranked by relevance, established influence, and distinct contribution; recent preprints are not ranked by their own state-of-the-art claims. GPTQ reconstructs layer outputs with second-order error compensation; GPTQv2 and Qronos address inherited errors. AWQ uses activation-informed scaling for weight-only compression. SpQR and OWQ preserve sensitive weights in higher precision, while SqueezeLLM combines nonuniform quantization with sparse storage. AQLM offers learned additive codebooks; QuIP# uses rotations and lattice codebooks. [AQLM’s related-work comparison](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.06118v3) directly supports these distinctions. Weight-only methods retain higher-precision activations; joint methods additionally quantize activations: [SmoothQuant](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10438) targets W8A8, while [QuaRot](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.00456) and [SpinQuant](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16406) target W4A4 and quantized KV caches. PTQ can include calibration-time optimization: QuIP# explicitly includes fine-tuning. Recent coverage includes 2025 reconstruction advances and 2026 curvature, outlier, and codebook proposals.
gaps: Search date: 2026-10-08; eight research calls used. Semantic Scholar search timed out and expansion lookups were throttled, limiting neighborhood coverage and citation completeness. Returned citation counts disagreed across providers and were not treated as precise rankings.

Recent dates distinguish first public preprints from later publication: SpinQuant and LRQ were publicly available before 2024-10-08 despite 2025 conference publication. The 2026 entries have verified indexed abstracts, but their full experiments and independent replication were not assessed.

Second-order limitations: layer-local calibration can miss inherited errors, motivating GPTQv2 and Qronos; equal output-channel weighting is challenged by KronQ. Sources: [GPTQv2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02692), [Qronos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11695), [KronQ](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07964).

Compression and deployment limitations: sparse high-precision exceptions and codebooks require storage beyond nominal weight indices. AQLM supplies kernels for specific encodings, so compression ratios alone do not establish general hardware speedups. Source: [AQLM representation and implementation](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.06118v3).

Codebook limitations: explicit vector-codebook size grows exponentially with dimension, motivating QTIP; imbalanced assignments can underutilize codewords, motivating BARQ. Sources: [QTIP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11235), [BARQ](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04490).

Accuracy limitations: SpinQuant reports up to 13 points of variation between random rotations. Scaling Laws for Precision links PTQ degradation to additional training data, but validates models only up to 1.7B parameters; extrapolation to much larger LLMs remains uncertain. Sources: [SpinQuant](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16406), [Scaling Laws for Precision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04330).

Coverage excludes quantization-aware pretraining, training-native binary models, and KV-cache-only methods. Targeted searches did not verify AutoRound or the intended HIGGS paper sufficiently for inclusion. Citation links are a verified subset from provider reference lists and inspected paper text; similarity and shared references were excluded.

answer.summary: GPTQ reconstructs layer outputs using second-order information; AWQ protects activation-sensitive channels through scaling. SpQR, OWQ, and SqueezeLLM handle sensitive weights using higher precision or non-uniform representations. AQLM and lattice/vector methods jointly encode weight groups, offering stronger extreme compression with more involved optimization and decoding. These approaches primarily compress weights while retaining higher-precision activations. SmoothQuant targets W8A8; QuaRot, SpinQuant, DuQuant, QUIK, and BCQ address low-bit activations too. This distinction matters because weight-only compression chiefly helps bandwidth-bound decoding, whereas quantizing both operands also addresses compute-bound prompt processing and batched inference. [QUIK](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09259) explains this workload distinction. Recent directions include accumulated-error correction, calibration-free scaling, and cheaper structured decoding. Rankings prioritize relevance and established influence; recent preprints remain provisional. The recent window uses first public release dates, so later conference publication does not turn an older method into a new contribution.
gaps: Second-order reconstruction has an accumulated-error limitation: GPTQv2 identifies mismatched upstream activations in GPTQ calibration and introduces asymmetric targets. [GPTQv2](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.02692v1)

Nominal bit widths are not complete storage measurements: SpQR, OWQ, and QUIK retain selected values in higher precision. Compare effective bits including metadata and exceptions. [SpQR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.03078), [OWQ](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02272), [QUIK](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09259)

Explicit vector codebooks grow exponentially with dimension; QTIP motivates trellis coding around this limitation. XOR-Trellis additionally identifies dequantization throughput and transformation cost as deployment challenges. [QTIP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11235), [XOR-Trellis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00432)

Post-training does not always mean optimization-free: QuIP# includes fine-tuning, SpinQuant learns rotations, and OmniQuant learns quantization parameters. Their preparation costs should be separated from inference benefits.

Accuracy claims are configuration-dependent. ZeroQuant-V2 reports unrecovered quality in its tested low-bit regimes; SpinQuant reports substantial variation between random rotations. Neither establishes a universal failure threshold. [ZeroQuant-V2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08302), [SpinQuant](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16406)
No common benchmark or hardware-normalized comparison was verified across all 25 papers. Abstract-level evidence cannot establish a universal winner, especially for the newest 2026 preprints.

Coverage audit: searched as of 2026-10-08 using eight research operations, counting individual native search queries separately. Semantic Scholar search timeouts and citation-expansion throttling limited coverage; the citation list is verified but incomplete.

Quantization-aware pretraining, general QAT, pruning-only papers, and KV-cache-only compression were excluded. Mixed methods were included when post-training weight quantization was a central contribution.

answer.summary: Ordered by relevance and established methodological importance, rather than measured citation counts. GPTQ supplies second-order reconstruction; AWQ protects salient channels through activation-informed scaling; SpQR and SqueezeLLM separate outliers; QuIP/QuIP# spread extremes through rotations; AQLM learns additive codebooks. [AQLM’s comparison](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.06118#S2.SS1) connects these approaches. Calibration activations do not imply activation quantization: most listed compression methods are weight-only. [SmoothQuant](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10438) instead targets W8A8, while [LRQ](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.393/) evaluates both categories. [D²Quant](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02546) addresses activation drift even when activations remain floating point. Recent entries include a 2025 conference publication and two 2026 papers; VPTQ’s September 2024 appearance precedes the requested window.
gaps: Calibration generalization: AWQ reports that GPTQ reconstruction can overfit calibration data and distort features on other domains. This is the authors’ comparative finding, not a universal result. [AWQ §1](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.00978#S1)
Scaling tradeoff: AWQ shows that excessive salient-channel scaling can enlarge the quantization step and increase errors on other channels. [AWQ §3.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.00978#S3.SS2)

Sub-4-bit reliability remains model-dependent: D²Quant identifies sensitive down-projections and quantization-induced activation drift as continuing bottlenecks. [D²Quant abstract and introduction](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02546)

Compression versus implementation cost: AQLM discusses runtime complexity in extreme quantization; its encoding also requires codebook storage and approximate discrete optimization. Compare total stored bytes and measured latency, not nominal weight bits alone. [AQLM §§1–3](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.06118)

Speedup depends on deployment: AWQ uses weight packing, fused kernels and on-the-fly dequantization to realize gains. Weight-only results do not establish equivalent acceleration for compute-heavy workloads or joint low-bit arithmetic. [AWQ §§1–2](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.00978)

Task coverage: the recent code-generation study examines two model families and Python/Java benchmarks; its method ranking should not be generalized to all reasoning, languages or long-context tasks. [Study abstract](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14181)

Search coverage is selective under the eight-call limit, especially for 2025–2026 follow-ups. LRQ’s 2025 conference date was verified, but its first-preprint date was not; empty quote fields indicate that the listed paper’s own text was not inspected.

answer.summary: GPTQ reconstructs layer outputs using approximate second-order information; AWQ uses activation-guided scaling; SpQR and SqueezeLLM preserve exceptional weights separately; AQLM jointly encodes weight vectors with additive codebooks, while QuIP# uses incoherence processing and lattice codebooks. These relationships are described in [AQLM’s related work](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.06118). They are weight-only approaches: using activations for calibration does not mean quantizing activations. [SmoothQuant](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/xiao23c.html) instead targets W8A8. Recent [D²Quant](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02546) corrects activation drift while retaining weight-only quantization; [LRQ](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.393/) evaluates both regimes. The order prioritizes relevance and foundational significance, rather than measured citation counts.
gaps: Recent coverage is incomplete: the eight-operation research budget verified D²Quant’s 2026 preprint and LRQ’s 2025 conference publication, but did not establish an exhaustive 2024-10-08–2026-10-08 shortlist. LRQ is included on publication date, without verification of its first preprint date.

Sub-4-bit accuracy remains a limitation. D²Quant identifies down-projection sensitivity and quantization-induced activation drift as bottlenecks; its mean correction removes systematic shift but leaves residual variance. [Source](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02546)

Compression does not establish portable acceleration. AQLM provides efficient kernels for specific encodings, so its reported speedups should not be generalized to every codebook configuration, device or workload. [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.06118)

Evaluation must extend beyond perplexity: the instruction-tuned-model study reports dependence on method, model size and task, including exceptions for instruction following and hallucination detection, and limited MT-Bench discrimination. [Source](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.11055)

Nominal bit-width alone is an incomplete comparison: sparse outlier formats and codebook formats encode different auxiliary information. A useful follow-up would compare total stored size and measured inference performance under matched conditions. This is an inference from the representations discussed in [AQLM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.06118).
